asks.text: How much stronger should each rarity be? I suggest ×1.41 per rarity: Common 10, Uncommon 14.1, Rare 20, Epic 28.3, Legendary 40, Mythic 56.6. Nobody's companion gets weaker, and none more than doubles. The other choices are today's ×2, which makes most companions 4× or 8× stronger, or keeping each companion's current damage, which makes new Commons and moved-up Uncommons hit the same.

Legendary has 14 companions, not 15. Should it open early? I suggest yes: 0.20% at Rift Level 5, rising to 1.00% at Level 46, with the 14 sharing it (Riftmourn 1.07% of Legendary). Otherwise Hollow Knight, Moonveil Stag, Stone Sentinel, Dusk Revenant and ten Realm 2 companions can't be summoned until a 15th Legendary exists.

Forgotten Watcher is the only Mythic. I suggest leaving it unsummonable until Mythic has 15 companions, as your request says. Players who own it keep it. The other choice is keeping it Legendary for now, but then Legendary would have two Aberrations.

What should a level cost for the new rarities? I suggest multipliers of Epic 5, Legendary 8 and Mythic 13, rising at the same pace as Uncommon to Rare. Without these, Epic and higher companions can't be levelled at all.
Which three new Commons should new players choose their starter from? I suggest Brackenfox, Burrbloom and Tackbolt: a Beast, a Wildgrowth and a Construct, like today's three.

The save update in the plan: it recalculates each companion's Essence so its level stays the same, moves Auto's stop choices, and adds a marker that it ran. I suggest building it last, after #119, #78, #89 and #97, and testing it on a made-up full save first.
The summon roll needs finer steps: parts per million instead of parts per 10,000. Riftmourn at Level 5 is 21 per million, which is less than one step today. That change is in ownership-v5.js.
New saves would store the starter by companion name ID (starterId), because today's starter number only reaches today's three starters. Old saves keep theirs as they are.

#78 as built keeps today's five Tome tables and adds no new rarities. So the only chance table that covers all ten rarities is #97's draft ladder, and I used it. If you change the ladder in #97, this plan follows it.

Moving companions up a rarity makes each of them rarer to summon, because each rarity is summoned less often. For example, Hollow Knight goes from about 0.5% today to about 0.02% at Level 5. That's what moving up means, but you'll notice it.
